passage: Creche note, Thursday. Farhan has just turned one and joined our room this month. This week I noticed him light up with a wide smile, mouth open, when I bent over his mat, and again when the cook, Mala, called his name from the door. Each time I smiled back and said, “Hello, Farhan,” and he answered with a gurgle, then looked at me again as if waiting. I will keep greeting him face to face at his level. 🙂 Ganga

qa.q: Who wrote the note, and when?
qa.a: Ganga, signing at the end, wrote the creche note on Thursday.

qa.q: What might Farhan's wide smile and waiting look mean?
qa.a: Probably pleasure and a wish to keep the exchange going, since he smiled, gurgled and looked back at her. He might also just be reacting to a friendly tone of voice.

qa.q: What is Ganga's plan and why might it work?
qa.a: She will greet him face to face at his level. Smiling back gives him a response, which helps him learn that his signals get answered.

qa.q: How might Mala's greeting feel to Farhan?
qa.a: Hearing his name from a familiar voice can feel welcoming, so he smiles at her too, showing he already links her with warmth.

grounding: A young child gives broad social smiles to familiar faces, and the adult's returned smile builds the exchange.

passage: On the verandah in the afternoon light, Swati sat with her baby Yogesh in her lap, wiping his face after his rice. He looked up at her and his mouth opened into a huge, gummy smile, arms waving. Swati smiled back and tilted her head. “Oh, is that for me?” Yogesh cooed and smiled again, watching her eyes. Her mother-in-law, passing with a basket, grinned at the pair. Swati waited a beat, then said his name softly and got another smile in return, like a small back-and-forth.

qa.q: What was Swati doing when Yogesh smiled at her?
qa.a: She was wiping his face after his rice while he sat in her lap on the verandah.

qa.q: What does Yogesh seem to feel when he smiles at Swati?
qa.a: He seems pleased and connected to her, since he waves his arms and keeps watching her eyes. It could also be a response to her friendly voice, not yet a message meant for her.

qa.q: Why does Swati's smiling back matter?
qa.a: It shows him that his signal gets an answer, and it starts a conversation of attention. She can keep taking small turns with him.

qa.q: How might Swati's mother-in-law see the moment?
qa.a: She may see a mother and baby learning each other, and it may bring back memories of her own children's first smiles.

grounding: A young child gives a broad open-mouth smile to a familiar face, and the mother's smile back builds the early back-and-forth.

passage:
Jamal lay on the play mat by the window of their small flat in Marseille. Nour leaned over him, close enough for him to see her clearly. "Hello, Jamal," she sang.
For a moment he just stared. Then his mouth opened wide and a big gummy smile spread across his face. Nour smiled back and cooed. Jamal kicked his legs and smiled again, then made a soft "ah". Nour answered, "Ah!" He waited, and smiled once more.

qa.q: Where was Jamal lying?
qa.a: On the play mat by the window of their small flat in Marseille.

qa.q: What does Jamal's wide, gummy smile suggest?
qa.a: It suggests pleasure and a growing connection with Nour, since he smiled after seeing her face and again when she answered; it might partly be the light from the window, but repeating it with her points to her.

qa.q: What did Nour do that helped the exchange keep going?
qa.a: She smiled back, cooed and copied his "ah", then waited, which turned his smile into a little back-and-forth conversation.

qa.q: How is the moment likely to feel for Nour?
qa.a: Probably joyful and tender, because the baby is answering her smiles for the first time.

grounding: An infant's broad open-mouth social smile at a familiar face, answered by the caregiver to build an early conversation.

passage:
I'm Naveen, and I'm Hansa's big brother. For weeks my baby sister only smiled at Amma. With me she just stared, like I was a wall.
Yesterday I leaned over her cot after school and made my silly cluck sound. She stared. I did it again and smiled at her. Then she opened her mouth wide and smiled back, a big one. I don't know if she knew it was me or just liked the cluck. I stayed and did it ten more times.

qa.q: What sound did Naveen make over Hansa's cot?
qa.a: He made his silly cluck sound.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling before Hansa smiled at him?
qa.a: He felt left out, because for weeks she only smiled at Amma and just stared at him "like I was a wall". Her smile likely made him delighted.

qa.q: What could Naveen keep doing to get more smiles?
qa.a: He can keep leaning in close, smiling and making the same sound, then waiting for her to answer.

qa.q: How might Hansa experience Naveen's repeated clucks and smiles?
qa.a: She is likely enjoying a familiar, friendly face and sound, and each smile back teaches her that her smile gets a response.

grounding: An older brother's account of a baby's first broad smile at him, answered with smiles to build connection.

passage:
First visit: Arohi Masi leaned over the cot and sang. Baby Preeti only watched her with a solemn face.
The next Sunday: Arohi came again with the same song. Preeti's mouth twitched at the corners, a tiny half-smile, then she looked away.
Two weeks later: as soon as Arohi's face appeared above the cot, Preeti's mouth opened in a wide, delighted smile. Arohi smiled back and said, "There you are!" Preeti smiled again and gurgled.

qa.q: What did Preeti do on the first visit?
qa.a: She only watched Arohi with a solemn face.

qa.q: How can you tell Preeti had come to feel happy seeing Arohi?
qa.a: By the third visit she smiled wide and delighted as soon as Arohi's face appeared, and gurgled when Arohi smiled back, showing pleasure and recognition.

qa.q: Which of Arohi's choices worked over the visits?
qa.a: Coming back with the same song and answering each smile helped Preeti get used to her face.

qa.q: If Arohi had given up after the first solemn stare, what might have changed?
qa.a: Preeti would have had fewer chances to learn her face, and the smile might have taken longer to come.

grounding: Over three visits a baby's solemn look grows into a broad social smile at a familiar aunt, who smiles back.

passage:
Naveen unlocked the door of the flat, bag still on his shoulder, traffic horns fading behind him. Aditi was in her high chair, mashing rice with her fist.
She saw him and her whole mouth opened into a huge smile.
Naveen grinned back. “Hello, you!”
She smiled again, kicked her legs, made a gurgle.
He leaned closer and smiled, and waited. She smiled, and waited too.
They kept it up, smile for smile, until her rice was cold.

qa.q: What was Aditi doing in her high chair when Naveen came in?
qa.a: She was mashing rice with her fist.

qa.q: What was Aditi feeling when she gave Naveen a huge open-mouthed smile?
qa.a: She seems pleased and happy to see a familiar face, and her kicking legs show excitement too.

qa.q: Why was Naveen's response a good one?
qa.a: By smiling back and waiting for her turn, he started a little back-and-forth conversation that builds their connection.

qa.q: What would change if Naveen had walked past to his phone?
qa.a: Aditi's smile would get no answer, and the playful back-and-forth would not happen.

grounding: It shows a young child giving a broad smile to a familiar face and a parent smiling back, starting an early conversation of attention.
